rationale: A wins because it knows where to stop: "Airtable just gave AI agents write access to enterprise data. What happens when one gets it wrong?" is hard, grounded, and paired with the right hold-until-proof warning. B has real instincts, but "employees are the ones left to catch what they get wrong" and "send communications" wander past the facts; that is how a decent angle gets a fact-check bruise before it leaves the building.
gaps_in_A: "pre-AI decacorns rebrand to survive" imports a broader survival-pressure frame not proven by the update. It may be a valid business-press lens, but it needs outside evidence.
"formally retiring the 'spreadsheet-database' identity" overstates the supplied fact, which says Airtable is shifting messaging. Retiring is stronger than shifting.

"write access to enterprise data" is mostly supported by updating statuses, but the email example is only drafting, not sending. Keep the risk language tied to records unless Airtable confirms outbound action.
gaps_in_B: "send communications" invents a capability. The update says agents draft emails, not send them.
"employees are the ones left to catch what they get wrong" invents the human fallback workflow. No notification, approval, audit, or review burden is in the facts.
The fourth workplace angle is the governance angle in softer clothes. It has a different protagonist, but the same unsupported reliability hole does all the work.

"All four angles are blocked on the same gaps" is too blunt. The valuation and positioning angles need exec/valuation proof; the reliability and workplace angles need reliability/customer workflow proof. Those are not the same blockade.
